title: An Afternoon in the Archive
paragraphs: During an afternoon at a community archive, a class examined records of ordinary experiences. Some came from personal journals, while others resembled reports or scenes from fiction. The students agreed that useful evidence could come from a quiet incident as well as a surprising one.

Several records provided a starting point for the discussion. The teacher calmed the unruly class before beginning the lesson. A vast desert stretched beyond the mountains. Local farmers vend fresh fruit at the weekend market. The market was a vibrant place filled with music and color.

Other records complicated that first impression and encouraged a closer reading. The final goal secured victory for the home team. Patience is a virtue that helps during difficult work. The critic launched a virulent attack on the author's character. The deer remained wary of the unfamiliar sound.

When the group returned to its original question, the discussion had become more precise. The members could point to particular actions and details instead of relying on a vague impression. They did not force every account to teach the same lesson. Their final display invited readers to compare the evidence, explain a connection, and consider where that connection ended.

targets.definition: extremely large in size or extent
full of energy, life, or strong color
success in a contest or struggle
a morally good quality or habit
careful because of possible danger or trouble
